common_name: Austrian Crescent Potato (Nutty Yellow-Fleshed Heirloom Fingerling)

planting.note: Plant seed potato pieces with 2-3 eyes per piece in cool soil; Austrian Crescent is a late-season heirloom fingerling. In zone 9, plant January-February for a spring harvest before summer heat arrives.

directions: Plant seed potato pieces 3-4 inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil, hilling as vines grow; harvest when vines begin to die back. Austrian Crescent is a classic heirloom fingerling potato with tan-gold skin and yellow, waxy flesh, prized for its rich, buttery, nutty flavor that many consider among the best-tasting of the fingerling types. Tubers grow in a distinctive curved, crescent shape, and the plant is a reliable, moderately high-yielding producer. As with other fingerlings, the low-starch, waxy texture holds its shape well through boiling, roasting, and potato salad preparations rather than becoming mealy or falling apart. Because it is a later-maturing variety, allow it a longer season than early potatoes; harvest for new potatoes once flowering finishes, or wait for full maturity and vine dieback for larger tubers with better storage life.

common_name: Rose Finn Apple Potato (Rose-Skinned Heirloom Fingerling)

planting.note: Plant seed potato pieces with 2-3 eyes per piece in cool soil; Rose Finn Apple is a late-season Scandinavian heirloom fingerling. In zone 9, plant January-February for a spring harvest before summer heat arrives.

directions: Plant seed potato pieces 3-4 inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil, hilling as vines grow; harvest when vines begin to die back. Rose Finn Apple is a Scandinavian heirloom fingerling potato with rose-pink to tan skin and creamy yellow flesh, valued for its smooth, dense, waxy texture and sweet, rich flavor that holds up especially well in roasting and potato salads. The elongated, knobby tubers form in loose clusters and the plant is a dependable, moderately productive grower. Being a later-maturing variety, it benefits from a full growing season; dig for tender new potatoes once flowering finishes, or let the vines die back naturally for mature tubers with better storage qualities. Like other fingerlings, its low-starch flesh keeps its shape well through cooking rather than turning mealy.

common_name: Magic Molly Potato (Deep Purple High-Anthocyanin Potato)

planting.note: Plant certified seed potato pieces 4-6 weeks before last frost in cool soil; Magic Molly is a late-season, high-anthocyanin purple potato. In zone 9, plant January-February for a spring harvest before summer heat arrives.

directions: Plant certified seed potato pieces 10-12 inches apart, 3-4 inches deep, in fertile, well-drained soil, hilling twice as plants grow to boost yield and prevent tuber greening. Magic Molly is a striking purple potato with deep violet-black skin and vivid, uniform purple flesh throughout, prized for its exceptionally high anthocyanin content, dense, moist texture, and rich, earthy flavor that some describe as slightly nutty. Unlike some older blue and purple varieties, Magic Molly holds its intense color well through cooking, making mashed potatoes a striking lavender-purple and roasted wedges deep violet inside. The medium-sized, round-to-oval tubers form in good numbers per plant, and the variety performs reliably across a range of climates. Harvest for new potatoes once flowering finishes, or wait until vines die back for full-sized, better-storing tubers.

planting.note: Plant certified seed potato pieces 4-6 weeks before last frost in cool soil; Bintje is a late-season, high-yielding Dutch heirloom potato dating to the early 20th century. In zone 9, plant January-February for a spring harvest before summer heat arrives.

directions: Plant certified seed potato pieces 10-12 inches apart, 3-4 inches deep, in fertile, well-drained soil, hilling twice as plants grow. Bintje is a classic Dutch potato bred in 1904 and, for much of the 20th century, one of the most widely grown potato varieties in Europe, prized for its pale yellow, moderately starchy flesh, excellent all-purpose cooking qualities, and reliable, heavy yields. It is especially well regarded for frying — Bintje is a traditional choice for Belgian and French fries — while also performing well boiled, mashed, or roasted, making it one of the more versatile heirloom varieties available. Tubers have smooth, light tan skin and store reasonably well after curing. Harvest for new potatoes once flowering finishes, or let vines die back fully for mature tubers with the best storage life and frying quality.
